content:
In the ever-evolving world of generative AI, we’re now empowered to bring our imagination to life with just a few words. But what if you could take that a step further—by specifying the exact environment and lighting condition for your scene?

Welcome to the Dynamic Scene Generator — a sleek and intuitive Streamlit app that lets you generate high-quality images using OpenAI's image generation model, with fine-tuned control over scene environments and lighting conditions.

🔧 Under the Hood: How It Works

The app is built using:

  • 🐍 Python
  • 🎨 Streamlit for the UI
  • 🤖 OpenAI’s Image Generation API
  • 🖼️ Pillow for image processing
  • 🌐 Requests for fetching the image
  • ✅ Certifi to ensure secure HTTPS communication

It allows users to:

  • Enter a custom scene description
  • Choose from various environments like Forest, Mountain, Ocean, etc.
  • Pick specific lighting conditions such as Dramatic Sunset, Neon Night, or Soft Morning Light
  • Select desired image resolution

🚀 Features

🎯 Prompt Customization

Users provide a scene prompt—anything from “a futuristic city” to “a cozy cabin”—and then enrich it with context like:

  • Environment: Is your city nestled in the mountains or on a snowy plain?
  • Lighting: Should the scene glow under natural daylight, shimmer in neon night, or burn with a dramatic sunset?

Example Prompt:

"A modern skyscraper by the ocean"
becomes:
"A modern skyscraper by the ocean in a Mountain environment under Dramatic Sunset"

🖼️ Image Generation & Display

Once the user hits Generate Image, the app sends the custom prompt to OpenAI’s API. The generated image is:

  • Fetched securely using requests + certifi
  • Displayed immediately within the Streamlit interface
  • Ready for download as a PNG file

💻 Code Snapshot

Here’s a simplified structure of the app:

prompt = "A modern skyscraper by the ocean"
environment = "Mountain"
lighting = "Dramatic Sunset"
full_prompt = f"{prompt} in a {environment} environment under {lighting}"
response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size="1024x1024")

This modularity makes it easy to expand or adapt to other use-cases like product staging, scene mockups, or concept art generation.

🎨 Real-World Applications

This app can be a game-changer for:

  • Concept artists: Instantly visualize mood boards
  • Content creators: Generate custom thumbnails or backdrops
  • Marketers: Create engaging visuals for campaigns
  • Game designers: Prototype game environments effortlessly
  • Educators: Showcase environmental effects in visual storytelling

🛠️ Get Started

To run this app locally:

  1. Install required packages:
    pip install streamlit openai pillow requests certifi
  2. Create an apikey.py file that stores your OpenAI key:
   apikey = "your-openai-api-key"
  1. Run the app using Streamlit:
   streamlit run your_script_name.py

🌟 Final Thoughts

AI is no longer just a tool for automation—it's becoming a co-creator. With this Dynamic Scene Generator, you're not just generating images; you're crafting visual experiences tailored to mood, setting, and lighting.

Try it out. See your imagination brought to life—one scene at a time.

Python Code:

import os

import certifi
import streamlit as st
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey  # Store your OpenAI key in apikey.py
import requests
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

# Set up the OpenAI API key
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

# Define environments and lighting conditions
environments = ["Mountain", "Ocean", "Forest", "Desert", "Urban", "Island", "Snowy"]
lighting_conditions = ["Natural Daylight", "Soft Morning Light", "Dramatic Sunset", "Neon Night", "Overcast", "Harsh Noon Light", "Dappled Sunlight"]

# Streamlit UI setup
st.title("Dynamic Scene Generator with Environmental and Lighting Controls")
st.write("Create AI-generated images based on specific environments and lighting conditions for detailed scene creation.")

# User input: Prompt, Environment, Lighting, and Image Size
prompt = st.text_input("Enter the scene prompt:", "A modern skyscraper by the ocean")
environment = st.selectbox("Select an environment:", environments)
lighting = st.selectbox("Select lighting conditions:", lighting_conditions)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

if st.button("Generate Image"):
    # Combine the inputs into a full prompt
    full_prompt = f"{prompt} in a {environment} environment under {lighting}"
    st.write(f"Generating image for: '{full_prompt}'")

    # Generate the image
    response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)
    image_url = response.data[0].url

    # Fetch and display the image
    img_response = requests.get(image_url,verify=certifi.where())
    img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))

    st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Image: {full_prompt}", use_column_width=True)

    # Provide an option to download the image
    img_bytes = BytesIO()
    img.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
    img_bytes.seek(0)
    st.download_button(label="Download Image", data=img_bytes, file_name=f"{environment.lower().replace(' ', '_')}_{lighting.lower().replace(' ', '_')}.png", mime="image/png")
